clue.text: Walker's way of going round with top hat off

indicators.note: the letters go round, turning about into a new order
off here means out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's habit of walking about with their tall hat removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top hat off' reads as removing a hat, but 'off' and 'going round' both signal rearrangement; the definition is the walker's route.
explanation.definitionFit: A path made for pedestrians is literally the route a person on foot takes.

clue.text: Arrangement for floor covering to follow

indicators.note: to follow places the covering after the first word

parts.note: taken as written
a mat covers a floor

explanation.surface: Deciding the layout for carpeting to come next.
explanation.definitionFit: The layout or design of something is its overall arrangement.

clue.text: Instruction manual shows customers' supply requirements

parts.note: an order is a command or instruction
a manual is a book of instructions

explanation.surface: A handbook sets out what clients need delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's list of outstanding purchase requests records what clients need supplied.

clue.text: Pressman who takes snap decisions when visualising stories

definitions.text: Pressman who takes snap decisions when visualising stories

parts.words: Pressman who takes snap decisions when visualising stories
parts.note: a news worker who chooses the photographs (snaps) that illustrate reports

explanation.surface: A reporter making hasty choices while imagining tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap decisions' suggests haste, but a snap is a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A press photographer tells news stories through images, choosing which shots to take.

clue.text: I'm going in to add your old boy's name

indicators.note: going in places the letters of I'm inside the word to

parts.note: taken as written
I'm gives its letters without the apostrophe
thy is the old form of 'your'

explanation.surface: Someone joining to add a name for their former son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' reads as entering a room, but it sets I'm inside 'to'; 'your old' is the archaic form of your.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional male given name, as borne by the biblical companion of Paul.

clue.text: Suppress sudden attacks about the French

indicators.note: about signals that the word for sudden attacks is turned round

parts.note: fits are sudden attacks of illness or temper
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Holding back sudden assaults concerning the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it turns the word for sudden attacks backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother or hold back something is a synonym of suppressing it.

clue.text: Someone providing great support for someone who pulls muscle?

explanation.surface: A strong helper and a person who strains a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes a tower as one who tows, so a tower of strength drags strength along; 'pulls muscle' suggests an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A dependable person is called this idiom, and literally one who tows (a tower) power along.

clue.text: A Highland dance can be a wild occasion

explanation.surface: A Scottish dance can turn into a riotous evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highland fling is a Scottish dance, and the word also means a short spell of wild enjoyment.

clue.text: They put bums in seats by exercising their franchise

definitions.text: They put bums in seats by exercising their franchise

parts.words: They put bums in seats by exercising their franchise
parts.note: people who vote place politicians, here called bums, into parliamentary seats by using their right to vote

explanation.surface: Fans fill a stadium by using their sports franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put bums in seats' sounds like filling a theatre, and 'franchise' like a business licence, but it is the right to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters use their franchise, the right to vote, to send candidates to parliamentary seats.

clue.text: Caught some working in ravine

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
any means some, as in 'have you any?'
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Some people found working down in a gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, narrow gorge is a synonym of a canyon-like valley.

clue.text: Where cowboys show off, sat on back of pinto

parts.note: a rider sat on a horse rode it

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here the end of pinto

explanation.surface: A cowboy perched on a spotted horse, ready to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: A pinto is a piebald horse, so the surface stays in the cowboy world while giving only its last letter, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is the arena event where ranch hands display riding and roping skills.

clue.text: Intend what sounds like trickery at the same time

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it

indicators.note: signals that the next word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: a wile is a cunning trick

explanation.surface: Planning something that seems deceptive, all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means during the same period, a synonym of simultaneously.

clue.text: Atmosphere good: OK for flying

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us
worthy means good or deserving

explanation.surface: A weather report: conditions fine, so planes may take off.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft certified safe to fly is described with this term.

clue.text: Just a political designation? Correct

explanation.surface: Is a political label merely accurate?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fair (just), names the conservative wing in politics, and means accurate (correct).

clue.text: Insignificant person, associated with a popular diarist

explanation.surface: A minor figure linked to a famous journal-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody (1892) is a comic British novel by George and Weedon Grossmith, kept by the clerk Charles Pooter.
explanation.definitionFit: An unimportant person is called this, and the word appears in the title of Pooter's fictional diary.

clue.text: Nitre, if shaken about, is quicker

indicators.note: shaking the letters about mixes them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: saltpetre, if agitated, reacts faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'quicker', with 'is' as a link: nifty means agile or quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty means deft and fast-moving, so the comparative means more nimble or speedier.

clue.text: To start with this month I need an opening

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old letter-writing
taken as written
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: To begin with, I require a gap this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is an old commercial abbreviation for 'of this month'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something in motion or provoke it is to start it.

clue.text: Very attractive woman bowling to spectator

parts.note: a looker is slang for a good-looking person
a cricketer who is bowling is on

explanation.surface: A glamorous woman at the bowls club watching from the side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler who is bowling is 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who watches without taking part is an onlooker, an observer.

clue.text: Or take original English source of timber

indicators.note: original suggests something novel, so the letters are made new by rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to choose the first English version.
explanation.definitionFit: This hardwood tree is a classic supplier of wood for building and furniture.

clue.text: Urge club leader to get up. Breakfast could be here!

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so take the first letter of club

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Encouraging the club captain to rise for the morning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a boiled egg for breakfast sits in this holder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled egg is served in this small cup at the morning meal.

clue.text: Start is temporarily delayed to accommodate designer

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, as a host accommodates a guest

explanation.surface: A launch is put back for a while to fit in a creative person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delayed' completes the surface reading; the answer sits inside 'stART IS Temporarily'.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer is a creative practitioner, an example of someone working in the visual arts.

clue.text: Unprofessional element of bedlam at European summit

indicators.note: an element is a part of the following words, so the answer is taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Chaos breaks out at a summit of European leaders, which looks inexpert.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'bedlAM AT EURopean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without professional training or pay works as a non-professional.

clue.text: A serious offence to catch both going over the game

indicators.note: both pieces are turned over, read backwards as one run

parts.note: a sin is a grave moral wrong
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: A grave crime of snaring both parties goes over the line.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN then NET reversed together gives TENNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: It's in order to return to Alabama for this marsupial

indicators.note: returning means the word for 'in order' is read backwards

parts.note: OK means all in order
Ala is the abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: Everything is fine for a trip back to Alabama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian tree-dwelling animal carries its young in a pouch, the mark of the marsupial group.

clue.text: Curved tip of cue splits a snooker ball

indicators.note: splits means it breaks the ball's word open to sit inside

parts.note: a red is one of the snooker balls

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here of cue

explanation.surface: A cue tip striking and splitting a snooker ball.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside RED, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent in the shape of a bow is to be curved.

clue.text: Bush telegraph reveals where fruit for Bordeaux comes from

definitions.text: where fruit for Bordeaux comes from

explanation.surface: Rumour reveals the origin of wine-making fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush telegraph' is informal word of mouth; the second reading is the plant that bears the fruit of Bordeaux wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal rumour networks are called this, and literally a vine bears wine grapes.

clue.text: Reportedly ruined it due strangely to moral correctness

indicators.note: signals that a word is replaced by how it is pronounced

parts.note: something ruined is wrecked

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the following words are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rumour that a disaster was caused by odd circumstances bears on ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: WRECKED said aloud gives RECT; 'strangely' rearranges IT DUE to ITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprightness of behaviour is a formal synonym for moral correctness.

clue.text: Cereal crop is very small amount

explanation.surface: A crop that is only a tiny quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat and similar seeds are called this, and the word also means a tiny particle.

clue.text: Nothing on state can be untidy

indicators.note: can be says the letters may become another word when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wearing no clothes is a scruffy condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no clothes on is the condition of nakedness.

clue.text: Ran chess differently, knowing quality

indicators.note: doing it differently means arranging the letters in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ran a chess club in a new way, showing shrewdness.
explanation.definitionFit: A sly, knowing manner is described as roguish or mischievous, an abstract noun of that trait.
